title: Virtual fundamental classes, part II: integral and non-separated Chow theory of Deligne–Mumford stacks and virtual classes over general bases
summary: Integral Chow groups of Deligne–Mumford stacks of finite type over any field without separatedness, their degrees and integral operations; through the finite cover by a scheme that every such stack has, rational pushforward, Gysin maps and Chern classes on stacks; comparisons with the scheme, algebraic-space and separated rational groups; intersection rings, moduli spaces, the ring structure of the Edidin–Graham comparison and the closed formula for degrees of points; the virtual class without the resolution property or separatedness, the relative obstruction class and characterisations, relative formulas over pure-dimensional bases, relative invariance of the canonical rational equivalence on ambients neither smooth nor reduced, regular pullback and functoriality over bases of pure dimension, deformation invariance, and the perfect relative obstruction theory of relative spaces of maps from prestable curves.

layers.title: Proper covers, function fields and degrees

targets.name: StackChow.ProperCover
targets.statement: A proper cover of a stack M is a scheme X of finite type over k with a proper surjective (hence representable) morphism X -> M; for integral M a proper covering is one with X integral and X -> M generically finite. Every stack M has a finite, finitely presented surjective morphism Z -> M from a scheme of finite type over k, etale over a dense open substack, so every stack has a proper cover and every integral stack a proper covering; a stack with a separated finite-type morphism to a Noetherian scheme (in particular every separated stack) has a generically finite proper cover by a quasi-projective scheme; proper covers pass to closed and open substacks, along morphisms representable by schemes, to vector bundles and products, and from M' to M along a proper representable surjection M' -> M.
hypotheses: M a Deligne-Mumford stack of finite type over a field k with quasi-compact separated diagonal representable by schemes (Convention 1)

locator.where: Theorem B, lines 81-85 (attribution lines 86-87); vistoli1989 Lemma 1.10 and (1.11), lines 299-328, and lines 582-584; deligne-mumford1969 Theorem 4.12, lines 1012-1019; kresch1999b Remark 2.6, lines 307-315

api.name: ProperCover.finite_exists
api.statement: Every stack of Convention 1 has a finite, finitely presented surjective morphism from a scheme of finite type over k, etale over a dense open substack (rydh2015 Theorem B, lines 81-85).

api.name: ProperCover.restrict
api.statement: A proper cover of M restricts to closed and open substacks and to stacks representable by schemes over M, and composes with a proper representable surjection onto M.

api.name: ProperCover.covering_exists
api.statement: Every integral M has a proper covering (a dominating component of a finite cover, reduced); two proper coverings are dominated by an integral closed subscheme of their fibre product surjecting onto both (vistoli1989 lines 1610-1613).

api.name: ProperCover.of_separated
api.statement: A stack with a separated finite-type morphism to a Noetherian scheme has a generically finite proper cover by a quasi-projective scheme (deligne-mumford1969 Theorem 4.12).

tests.name: BG_finiteEtaleCover
tests.statement: Spec k -> BG is finite etale of degree |G|, a proper covering although BG has no dense open scheme for |G|>1.

tests.name: doubledOrigin_selfCover
tests.statement: The identity of the line with doubled origin is a proper cover; no separated scheme surjects properly onto it (valuative criterion with two extensions through the two charts).

tests.name: baseChange_nonRepresentable
tests.statement: Base change of id_{Spec k} along BG -> Spec k is id_BG, proper surjective but with non-scheme source.

tests.name: BG_nonseparatedGroup_finiteCover
tests.statement: For G the etale group over A^1 obtained from Z/2 by deleting the non-identity point over 0, the two charts Q = A^1 + A^1 -> L of the doubled-origin line form a G_L-torsor (Q x_L Q = Q + Q|_{t!=0} = Q x_{A^1} G), so L -> B_{A^1}G is finite etale of degree 2 = (e(BG)/e(L))[k(t):k(t)]: a proper cover of a non-separated stack with non-finite inertia. No separated scheme is a proper cover (the torsor would be finite etale of degree 2 over t != 0 and 1 over 0), so requiring X separated would exclude it.

targets.name: StackChow.functionField
targets.statement: For an integral stack V, k(V) is the colimit over nonempty open substacks of morphisms to A^1, a field finitely generated over k with trdeg = dim V, identified for an etale U -> V from an integral scheme with the rational functions on U with equal pullbacks to U x_V U; e(V) is the order of the automorphism group of a geometric point over the generic point, equal to the degree of the inertia over a dense open where it is finite etale; e(V) = 1 iff V has a dense open substack that is an algebraic space.
hypotheses: V an integral stack (Convention 1; integral closed substacks of gap closed-substacks-of-stacks)

api.name: functionField.pullback
api.statement: A dominant morphism of integral stacks induces k(G) -> k(F), functorial; open immersions induce isomorphisms.

api.name: functionField.quotient
api.statement: For a finite etale group G acting on an integral scheme X, k([X/G]) = k(X)^G.

api.name: genericStabiliserOrder.eq_sum_deg_inertia
api.statement: e(V) is the sum of deg(I/V) (1.3) over the irreducible components I of (I_V)_red dominating V; e is unchanged on dense open substacks.

tests.name: BG_values
tests.statement: k(BG) = k and e(BG) = |G|; e(B S_3) = 6.

tests.name: A1modMu2_generic
tests.statement: e([A^1/mu_2]) = 1 and k = k(x^2), while the closed substack B mu_2 has e = 2; the largest stabiliser would give 2.

tests.name: nonseparatedGroup_genericLarger
tests.statement: For B_{A^1}G of 1.1, e = 2 though the stabiliser at 0 is trivial.

tests.name: inertia_sumOfDegrees
tests.statement: I_{BG} = BG + BG for G = Z/2 (1+1 = 2); for S_3 the components B Z(c) have degrees 1, 3, 2 (sum 6); over Q, I_{B mu_3} has components of degrees 1 and (3/3)[Q(zeta_3):Q] = 2 (sum 3, two components); on [A^1/mu_2] the non-identity component lies over 0, does not dominate, and the sum is 1.

tests.name: realGerbe
tests.statement: For [Spec C/(Z/4)] over R, k = R and e = 2, not the order 4 of the acting group.

targets.name: StackChow.stackDegree
targets.statement: For a separated dominant morphism f : F -> G of integral stacks, deg(F/G) in Q>=0 is deg(F x_G V/V) for representable f (V etale over G integral; generic rank, 0 if not generically finite) and deg(U/G)/deg(U/F) in general (U etale over F integral affine); it is independent of choices, multiplicative, equal to (e(G)/e(F))[k(F):k(G)] with [E:K] = 0 for infinite extensions, positive iff dim F = dim G, integral for representable f, and invariant under dominant base change with integral fibre product.
hypotheses: f separated and dominant
F, G integral stacks, not necessarily separated

api.name: stackDegree.id
api.statement: deg(V/V) = 1, and deg of a separated etale morphism from an integral scheme U to V is e(V)[k(U):k(V)]; such a morphism is dominant (open), and separated whenever U is (for instance U affine), since the composite U -> U x_V U -> U x U is a closed immersion and the second map, a base change of the diagonal of V, is separated, so the diagonal of U -> V is a closed immersion.

api.name: stackDegree.representable_int
api.statement: For representable proper f and integral V in F, deg(V/f(V)) is an integer (used by 3.2).

tests.name: BG_degrees
tests.statement: deg(BG/Spec k) = 1/|G| and deg(Spec k/BG) = |G|; without the stabiliser ratio deg(Spec k/BG) = 1 contradicts the representable degree |G|.

tests.name: A1_toPoint_zero
tests.statement: A^1 -> Spec k has degree 0.

tests.name: coarseMap_mu2
tests.statement: [A^1/mu_2] -> A^1 has degree 1 and B mu_2 -> {0} has degree 1/2.

tests.name: charP_inseparable
tests.statement: For Z/p acting by y -> y + x in char p, V = [V(x)/(Z/p)] -> Spec k[y^p] has degree (1/p)p = 1 = p/p.

tests.name: frobenius
tests.statement: Frobenius t -> t^p on A^1 is representable of degree p.

tests.name: separatedMorphism_notStacks
tests.statement: A chart A^1 -> L of the line L with a doubled origin is an open immersion, separated, of degree 1 = e(L)[k(t):k(t)] although L is not separated; the etale surjection L -> A^1 is not separated, so deg(L/A^1) is outside the definition and the formula, which would give 1, does not apply.

targets.name: StackChow.Cycles
targets.statement: Z_i(M) is the free abelian group on integral closed substacks of dimension i; the cycle of a closed substack Z is sum m_V [V] with m_V the length at a generic point on an etale atlas, independent of choices; pullback to an etale atlas U identifies Z_i(M) with the cycles on U with equal pullbacks to U x_M U. No separatedness or proper cover is assumed.
hypotheses: M a stack (Convention 1)

api.name: cycleOfSubstack.integral
api.statement: [V] = 1 [V] for integral V; [Z] = [Z_red] iff Z is generically reduced along every component.

api.name: cycleOfSubstack.scheme
api.statement: For a scheme of finite type over k the descended cycle of a closed subscheme is its usual cycle.

tests.name: BG_cycles
tests.statement: Z_0(BG) = Z [BG] and Z_i(empty) = 0.

tests.name: doublePoint_multiplicity
tests.statement: [[V(x^2)/mu_2]] = 2 [B mu_2]; the reduced support would give 1.

tests.name: scheme_agreement

targets.name: StackChow.stackChowGroup
targets.statement: For integral V of dimension i+1, W of dimension i and phi in k(V)^x, ord_W(phi) is the order on an etale atlas at a generic point of W x_V U, independent of choices and additive; W_i(M) = sum over integral V of dim i+1 of k(V)^x, the boundary sends (V, phi) to div(phi), and A_i(M) := Z_i(M)/dW_i(M), A_i(M)_Q := A_i(M) (x) Q. No separatedness or proper cover is assumed.
hypotheses: M a stack (Convention 1)

api.name: ChowGroup.classMap
api.statement: The class map Z_i -> A_i is surjective with kernel dW_i.

api.name: ChowGroup.vanishing
api.statement: A_i(M) = 0 for i < 0 and i > dim M; A_{dim M}(M) is free on the top-dimensional components.

api.name: ChowGroup.disjointUnion
api.statement: A_i of a disjoint union is the direct sum; equivalences induce isomorphisms.

tests.name: BG_chow
tests.statement: A_0(BG) = Z, A_i(BG) = 0 otherwise; W_{-1}(BG) = k^x is nonzero with zero boundary.

tests.name: A1modMu2_torsion
tests.statement: A_0([A^1/mu_2]) = Z/2 generated by [B mu_2]: div(y) = 2[B mu_2] and div(P(y)) = [W] for every monic irreducible P != y, k[x]/P(x^2) being reduced.

tests.name: nonRationalPoint
tests.statement: Over Q, div(y^2+1) = [V(x^4+1)/mu_2]; linear polynomials alone miss this point.

targets.name: StackChow.stackChowGroup.comparisons
targets.statement: For a scheme X of finite type over k, Z_i, dW_i and A_i are Tau Ceti's cyclesOfDimension, RatEquiv and ChowGroup compatibly with class maps; for a quasi-separated algebraic space of finite type they are the cycles and CH_i of stacks-chow-spaces Definitions 3.1 and 15.1 with B = Spec k, delta = 0; for a separated stack, A_i(M) (x) Q is VirtualFundamentalClass §2.1's A_i(M)_Q compatibly with cycle classes.
hypotheses: X of finite type over k; for the last statement M separated

tests.name: separated_rational

targets.name: StackChow.flatPullback

api.name: flatPullback.comp
api.statement: (g f)^* = f^* g^* and id^* = id.

api.name: flatPullback.open
api.statement: For an open immersion, f^* is restriction.

api.name: flatPullback.closedSubstack
api.statement: f^*[Z] = [Z x_G F] for every closed substack Z, integral or not.

api.name: flatPullback.descent
api.statement: Along an etale surjection from a scheme, flat pullback on cycles is the descent injection of 2.1; on schemes it is SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.2's flat pullback.

tests.name: BG_atlas
tests.statement: pi : Spec k -> BG gives pi^*[BG] = [Spec k]; multiplying by the degree would give |G|.

tests.name: productWithLine

tests.name: coarseFibre_nonreduced

targets.name: StackChow.properPushforward
targets.statement: For f : F -> G proper representable, f_*[V] := deg(V/f(V)) [f(V)] (integer, 0 when the dimension drops) carries dW_i(F) into dW_i(G), with f_* div(phi) = (e(f(V))/e(V)) div(N(phi)) when dim f(V) = dim V (N the norm of k(V)/k(f(V)); the factor an integer for representable f) and 0 otherwise, and induces f_* : A_i(F) -> A_i(G); integral.
hypotheses: f proper and representable

api.name: properPushforward.closedImmersion
api.statement: For a closed immersion, i_*[V] = [V].

api.name: properPushforward.div
api.statement: f_* div(phi) = (e(f(V))/e(V)) div(N(phi)) if dim f(V) = dim V, and 0 otherwise.

api.name: properPushforward.schemes
api.statement: On schemes, f_* is SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.2's proper pushforward with the weights of AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicCycle.map.

tests.name: BG_atlas_push

tests.name: noIntegralPushforward_BG

tests.name: P1_residueDegree
tests.statement: For P^1 -> Spec k, f_*[P] = [k(P):k][Spec k], SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.2.

tests.name: stabiliserFactor_div
tests.statement: For f : A^1 -> A^1 x BG (|G| > 1) and phi = t, f_* div(t) = |G|[0 x BG] while div(N(t)) = [0 x BG] since k(A^1 x BG) = k(t); the factor e(A^1 x BG)/e(A^1) = |G| is needed.

targets.name: StackChow.pushPull_and_localisation
targets.statement: For a 2-cartesian square with f proper representable and psi flat of relative dimension d, psi^* f_* = f'_* psi'^* on cycles and on A_*; for a closed substack Z with open complement U, A_i(Z) -> A_i(M) -> A_i(U) -> 0 is exact. Integral.

Z closed substack, U its complement

targets.name: StackChow.exteriorProduct
targets.statement: [V] x [W] := [V x_k W] passes to rational equivalence, giving A_i(F) (x) A_j(G) -> A_{i+j}(F x_k G); integral.
hypotheses: F, G stacks over k

api.name: exteriorProduct.assoc_comm
api.statement: Bilinear, associative, commutative up to the exchange isomorphism.

api.name: exteriorProduct.unit
api.statement: [Spec k] x a = a.

api.name: exteriorProduct.pushPull
api.statement: Commutes with flat pullback and proper representable pushforward in each factor.

api.name: exteriorProduct.schemes
api.statement: On schemes it is SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.5's exterior product.

tests.name: inseparableSquare

tests.name: BG_times_BH

targets.name: StackChow.refinedGysin
targets.statement: For a regular local immersion f : F -> G of codimension c of algebraic stacks locally of finite type and Y -> G from a quasi-separated algebraic space of finite type, f^![T] := (U -> X)_* s^*[C_{U/T}] defines f^! : A_i(Y) -> A_{i-c}(F x_G Y) integrally, compatible with proper pushforward and flat pullback along Y' -> Y, commuting for two regular local immersions, equal to s^*[C_{X/Y}] for equidimensional Y, and equal to SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.5's refined Gysin map for regular immersions of schemes.
hypotheses: f representable, unramified, of finite type, etale locally a regular closed immersion of codimension c
Y a quasi-separated algebraic space of finite type over k

api.name: refinedGysin.properPushforward
api.statement: f^! q_* = p_* f^! for q proper.

api.name: refinedGysin.flatPullback
api.statement: f^! q^* = p^* f^! for q flat.

api.name: refinedGysin.normalCone
api.statement: For Y equidimensional, f^![Y] = s^*[C_{X/Y}] (vistoli1989 Lemma 3.19).

api.name: refinedGysin.schemes
api.statement: For a regular immersion of schemes and Y a scheme, f^! is SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.5's refined Gysin map.

tests.name: zeroSection_selfIntersection
tests.statement: For the zero section of E over a scheme M, s^! inverts flat pullback and s^![M] = c_r(E) cap [M] (on P^1 with O(-1), -[pt]).

tests.name: doubleCover_origin
tests.statement: {0} -> A^1 refined along z -> z^2 gives 2[pt], the SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.5 Check.

tests.name: codimZero_BG

targets.name: StackChow.rationalPushforward
targets.statement: For f : F -> G proper, f_* : Z_i(F)_Q -> Z_i(G)_Q with Vistoli's rational degree induces f_* : A_i(F)_Q -> A_i(G)_Q, functorial, equal to 3.2 (x) Q for representable f; for proper surjective f, f_* is surjective on rational cycles and on rational equivalences (applied to a proper cover of F, 1.1); push-pull with flat morphisms holds rationally.
hypotheses: f proper

api.name: rationalPushforward.exteriorProduct
api.statement: For proper f : F' -> F and g : G' -> G, representable or not, (f x g)_*(a x b) = f_*a x g_*b on A_*(.)_Q with the exterior product of 3.4: write [V] x [W] = (deg(Y/V) deg(Y'/W))^{-1} (p x p')_*([Y] x [Y']) for proper coverings p : Y -> V, p' : Y' -> W (by 3.2 and 3.4; the degrees are positive), and apply 3.4 to the proper representable f p and g p' with functoriality.

api.name: rationalPushforward.surjective
api.statement: For proper surjective f, f_* is surjective on Z_*(.)_Q and on rational equivalences.

api.name: rationalPushforward.pushPull
api.statement: psi^* f_* = f'_* psi'^* on A_*(F)_Q for flat psi (vistoli1989 Lemma 3.9 (ii)).

api.name: rationalPushforward.div
api.statement: f_* div(phi) = (e(f(V))/e(V)) div(N(phi)) if dim f(V) = dim V, and 0 otherwise, with a rational factor.

tests.name: nonseparated_L_times_BZ2

targets.name: StackChow.stackGysin
targets.statement: For a regular local immersion f : F -> G of codimension c of algebraic stacks and any G' -> G from a stack, f^![V] := deg(Y/V)^{-1} r_*(f^![Y]) over proper coverings Y -> V, with f^![Y] 3.5's class on the algebraic space F x_G Y, defines f^! : A_i(G')_Q -> A_{i-c}(F x_G G')_Q, independent of coverings and compatible with rational equivalence; compatible with proper pushforward and flat representable pullback, equal to 3.5 (x) Q on algebraic spaces, commuting for two regular local immersions, with f^![G] = [F] for equidimensional G; flat pullback acts compatibly.
hypotheses: f a representable regular local immersion of codimension c
G' a stack (Convention 1)

api.name: stackGysin.flatPullback

api.name: stackGysin.fundamentalClass

api.name: stackGysin.algebraicSpace

targets.name: StackChow.stackChernClass
targets.statement: For a stack M and a vector bundle E of rank r with zero section s, pi^* : A_i(M)_Q -> A_{i+r}(E)_Q is an isomorphism with inverse s^!; Chern classes c_i(E), acting on A_*(G')_Q for every G' -> M from a stack through scheme Chern classes on proper coverings, satisfy c_0 = 1, vanishing above r, Whitney, additivity of c_1, the projection formula, commutation with flat representable pullback and Gysin maps, and s^! s_* = c_r(E) cap.
hypotheses: M a stack (Convention 1)
E a vector bundle of constant rank r

layers.title: Intersection rings, moduli spaces, quotients and points

targets.name: StackChow.intersectionProduct
targets.statement: For M smooth of pure dimension n, x . y := Delta^!(x x y) (Delta a regular local immersion of codimension n), and x ._f y := gamma_f^!(x x y) for f : F -> G with G smooth; A^*(M)_Q is a commutative associative graded Q-algebra with unit [M], flat representable pullback between smooth stacks is a ring map, g_*(g^*x . y) = x . g_*y for every proper g, with the pushforward of 4.1 (through (id x g)_* of exterior products, 4.1, and the commutation of 4.2's Gysin maps with proper pushforward), and on smooth schemes this is SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.6's product (x) Q. For smooth separated M of pure dimension and representable t : T -> M with T separated (equivalently t separated), every class in VirtualFundamentalClass §2.5's A^*(T -> M) commutes with all bivariant classes and evaluation on [M] is an isomorphism A^*(T -> M) = A_*(T)_Q.

targets.name: StackChow.moduliSpace_pushforward_iso
targets.statement: Let M be a stack and p : M -> M0 be proper onto a quasi-separated algebraic space of finite type inducing bijections on isomorphism classes of geometric points (a moduli space). Then V -> p(V) is a dimension-preserving bijection of integral closed substacks with integral closed subspaces (inverse N -> (N x M)_red); k(p(V)) in k(V) is purely inseparable; deg(V/p(V)) = [k(V):k(p(V))]/e(V), equal to 1/e(V) if k(p(V)) is perfect; p_* : A_i(M)_Q -> A_i(M0)_Q is an isomorphism; Keel-Mori coarse spaces of separated stacks are moduli spaces.
hypotheses: M a stack (Convention 1)
p proper, bijective on geometric points up to isomorphism
M0 quasi-separated algebraic space of finite type

targets.name: VirtualFundamentalClass.resolutionComparison
targets.statement: For two global resolutions F, H of a perfect E (isomorphisms in the derived category), P := F_1 x_E H_1 over the vector-bundle stack h1/h0(E^v) is a vector bundle of rank rk F_1 + rk H_0 = rk H_1 + rk F_0 with surjections onto F_1 and H_1 with kernels H_0 and F_0; it is the extension 0 -> H_0 -> P -> F_1 -> 0 pulled back from the H_0-torsor H_1, split on affine charts. No morphism of complexes between F and H is used.
hypotheses: E perfect of amplitude [-1,0] on a Deligne-Mumford stack
F, H global resolutions

hypotheses: Y algebraic stack locally of finite type, pure dimension d
X -> Y of Deligne-Mumford type, X a stack (Convention 1)
E perfect relative obstruction theory of constant rank r with a global resolution

T -> Tbar a square-zero extension of schemes over Y

layers.title: Base change and deformation invariance over bases of pure dimension

hypotheses: Y an algebraic stack locally of finite type over k
i : X -> Y a local immersion, v : Y' -> Y a regular local immersion
for invariance: Y' pulled back from a base B along a smooth morphism Y -> B of Deligne-Mumford type

targets.statement: For a cartesian square X' -> X over a local complete intersection morphism v : Z' -> Z of algebraic stacks over Y with finite unramified diagonal over Y, X and X' stacks of Convention 1, and perfect obstruction theories E, F with global resolutions compatible over v (VirtualFundamentalClass §§8.1, 9.5), v^![X/Y, E]^vir = [X'/Y, F]^vir when v is smooth, and when Z, Z' are smooth over Y, over any Y of pure dimension; v^! is flat pullback along u in the first case, and in the second flat pullback along Z'_0 x_Y X -> X followed by the Gysin map of the graph of v restricted to a quasi-compact open substack Z'_0 of Z' containing the image of X' (Z'_0 x_Y X is then a stack of Convention 1, which Z' x_Y X need not be), the composite being independent of Z'_0; the second case uses a cone comparison through the compatibility over v only, without a compatibility datum over the graph.
hypotheses: Y of pure dimension
v lci; smooth, or Z, Z' smooth over Y
E, F compatible over v, with global resolutions
X, X' stacks (Convention 1)
second case: Z'_0 a quasi-compact open substack of Z' containing g(X'); Y quasi-separated (Convention 7)

suppliers.what: The base roadmap: stack dimension, cones and normal cones, Vistoli's rational Chow theory of separated stacks with bivariant groups and the canonical rational equivalence, relative cotangent complexes, cone stacks and h1/h0, intrinsic normal cones, obstruction theories, the virtual class of separated stacks with the resolution property, compatible pullback and functoriality over smooth bases, and the relative class; through gap:closed-substacks-of-stacks, the integral closed substacks of its §2.1, and through gap:normal-cones-of-local-immersions, the normal cones and normal bundles of local immersions of its §1.5.

Algebraic spaces and stacks, inertia, points, separated and proper stacks, quotient stacks, coarse spaces and Keel–Mori, quasi-coherent cohomology and its topology comparison, derived categories, the upper shriek functor and relative dualising complexes, Riemann–Roch on curves, lifting for smooth morphisms, and the Chow theory of schemes.
The Edidin–Graham comparison A_{i-g}([X/G])_Q = A^G_i(X) (x) Q for Deligne–Mumford quotient stacks, with Chern classes and proper pushforward.
Equivariant Chow groups by Totaro's approximation, their operations and the equivariant product (Conventions 1, 4, 5).
Coherent cohomology and base change of proper curve families, the relative dualising sheaf, relative ampleness, prestable families.
Derived tensor and internal Hom on ringed sites, the pullback–pushforward adjunction, quasi-coherent derived sheaves and base change.
The naive truncation of the cotangent complex of a surjection, the smooth computation, and square-zero lifting obstructions for ring maps.

consumers.what: Its §§4.1–4.3 are the case of 9.3–9.5 over the prestable-curve stack with a smooth projective target in characteristic zero; 6.2 removes its use of the resolution property; 8.4 gives deformation invariance; 5.4 computes degrees on coarse spaces.

gaps.title: Closed, reduced and integral closed substacks of a Deligne–Mumford stack
gaps.detail: VirtualFundamentalClass §2.1 builds its cycles on integral closed substacks but its contract does not state their theory. Needed, with no separatedness: closed substacks as representable closed immersions up to equivalence, equivalently invariant closed subschemes of an étale presentation (vistoli1989 (1.5), lines 232–244); reduced, irreducible, integral ones (vistoli1989 (1.6), lines 245–250); the unique reduced closed substack on a closed subset of |M| (SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 Stacks.points) and the bijection of integral closed substacks with irreducible closed subsets; base change; images under proper morphisms and under flat morphisms (vistoli1989 (1.7), lines 254–269).
gaps.needs: VirtualFundamentalClass §2.1 must state the theory of closed, reduced and integral closed substacks of a Deligne–Mumford stack, with reduced induced structures, the support bijection, base change and images, without separatedness.

gaps.title: Normal cones of local immersions of algebraic stacks
gaps.detail: VirtualFundamentalClass §1.5 forms normal cones of representable closed immersions only; its §2.4 and 3.5, 4.2, 8.1 and 8.3 here use the normal cone of a local immersion (representable, unramified, of finite type) that need not be closed, such as Spec k -> BG or the diagonal BG -> BG x BG for a finite etale G with |G| > 1. Needed: the normal cone C_{X/Y} of a local immersion X -> Y of algebraic stacks locally of finite type over k, by descent from charts U -> V that are closed immersions of schemes with V -> Y and U -> X smooth surjective and U -> X x_Y V etale (kresch1999b Lemma 2.2 and the paragraph after it, lines 218-237; vistoli1989 Lemma 1.19 and lines 508-526), equal to §1.5's cone for closed immersions; for Y' -> Y, a closed embedding C_{X'/Y'} in C_{X/Y} x_X X', an isomorphism for flat Y' -> Y (vistoli1989 lines 529-535); the closed embedding in the normal sheaf; and, for a regular local immersion of codimension d, the equality with the normal bundle N_{X/Y} of rank d (vistoli1989 lines 527-528; kresch1999b lines 236-237).
gaps.needs: VirtualFundamentalClass §1.5 must state the normal cone C_{X/Y} of a local immersion X -> Y of algebraic stacks locally of finite type over k, obtained by descent from charts on which it is a closed immersion of schemes, with its closed embedding under base change (an isomorphism under flat base change), its closed embedding in the normal sheaf, and the normal bundle of a regular local immersion.
